parole.testo: From Proto-West Semitic *ʔalyat- (“fat tail, tail fat”). Cognate to Classical Syriac ܐܠܝܬܐ (ʾellīṯā) and Hebrew אַלְיָה ('alyá).
Inherited from Proto-West Semitic *him, from Proto-Semitic *šim.

parole.significato: to risk one's life, to defy death
parole.testo: From the root ق ت ل (q t l), from Proto-West Semitic *štaḳṭil-.
From Proto-West Semitic *baśar- (“flesh, human body”). The original meaning "flesh" was replaced by لَحْم (laḥm).
From Proto-West Semitic *baḳar- (“large cattle”). Cognate with Hebrew בָּקָר (baqár, “bovine, cattle, beef”), Aramaic בקרא, Phoenician 𐤁𐤒𐤓 (bqr) and Mehri بقريت (“cow”).
From Proto-Semitic *ṯql (“to weigh; burden, weight”). Cognate with Hebrew שקל and Aramaic תקל.

From Proto-West Semitic *gabbār-. Compare Hebrew גיבור / גִּבּוֹר (gibbōr) and Classical Syriac ܓܢܒܪܐ (ga(n)bbārā).
Inherited from Proto-West Semitic *ḫariʔ-.

parole.significato: a variety of dates (fruit and tree)
parole.testo: From Proto-West Semitic *daqal-, in Akkadian only found in the toponymy of Chaldean territory, and likewise the Arabic is suspect to be influenced by semantic loan from Aramaic דִקְלָא (diqlā, “date palm; topgallant”) for the sense of a “mast”, compare also سَارِيَة (sāriya, “post, mast”) from Arama
From the root ر و ح (r w ḥ), from Proto-West Semitic *rawaḥ-.

parole.significato: to bring ship near to the bank of a river, to land at a harbour, to dock
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-West Semitic *rpʔ (“to heal, protect”).
Etymologically related to Arabic: ريح (rīḥ, “wind”). From Proto-West Semitic *rūḥ-. Cognate with Hebrew רוּחַ (rúakh).
From Proto-West Semitic *rīḥ-.

parole.significato: to rush at, to spring upon to assault, to attack, to assail, to seize violently, to exact, to extract
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-West Semitic *saṭaw-.

parole.significato: the young of a deer or gazelle
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-West Semitic *ṭalay-.
From Proto-West Semitic *ʕigl-. Cognate with Hebrew עֵגֶל ('eguèl, “calf”).
From Proto-West Semitic *ʕaḏr- m (“help”, verbal noun). Cognates with Sabaean 𐩲𐩹𐩧 (ʿḏr, “excuse, pardon”) and Hebrew עזרה (ʿezrá, “help”).

parole.significato: a donkey; a wild ass; an onager
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-West Semitic *ʕayr-.

parole.significato: to kill, to slay, to murder
parole.testo: From Proto-West Semitic *ḳatal-. Cognate with Biblical Hebrew קָטַל (qɔṭal).

parole.significato: to say about to have said
parole.testo: From Proto-West Semitic *ḳawl- (“voice”). Cognate with Aramaic קָלָא (qālā, “sound; voice; noise”), Hebrew קוֹל (qōl, “sound; voice; noise”), and Ge'ez ቃል (ḳal, “sound; voice; speech; statement”).

parole.significato: to mark (symbols, shapes, graphs, glyphs, letters, and the like) on a surface, to write, to inscribe
parole.testo: From Proto-West Semitic *katab-, but the sense "to write" has long been considered a borrowing from another Central Semitic language, perhaps denominally from كِتَاب (kitāb).
From Proto-West Semitic *katip- f.
From Proto-West Semitic *laban-.

Inherited from Proto-West Semitic *milḥ-.

parole.significato: having partitive effect: of, some of, parts of, one of
parole.testo: From Proto-West Semitic *min. Cognate with Hebrew מִן (min).
From Proto-West Semitic *našr-, whence was derived the denominal root ن س ر (n s r).
From Proto-West Semitic *n-š-y. Compare Hebrew נָשָׁה (nashá, “to forget”) and Ge'ez ናሕሰየ (naḥsäyä).
